text: If an employee is injured working from home, where does employer liability end? Here's a quick guide from Clifford Gouldson Lawyers. An employer's duty of care is not diminished simply because work is performed from an employee's home. In a recent case, an employee tripped on a temporary puppy fence during an authorised break. On appeal, it was held that employment was not a significant contributing cause, so the employer avoided liability. Employers may wish to clearly define the work area, hours and expectations, and require periodic workspace self-assessments. If you're reviewing work from home arrangements, our team can help. Speak with Clifford Gouldson Lawyers.
